Try it: load spread in the replacement layer
The summary video of method group 1: the principles of lower contact pressure, a deeper foundation level and soil replacement step by step – with layer-by-layer compaction and load spread.

Two checks. Both the stress on the replacement layer at foundation level, σ1 = P/B, and the stress on the base layer at the bottom of the replacement layer, σ2 = P/(B + 2·v·tg ϑ) + γ1·v, must stay below the allowable value.
Backfilling. Sandy gravel, crushed stone or crushed concrete is spread and compacted in layers of at most 30 cm – above the water table.

Widening. On each side, the bottom of the excavation is v·tg ϑ wider than the footing: the load spreads at the angle ϑ, so at the bottom of the replacement layer it is distributed over a width of B + 2·v·tg ϑ.
Excavation. The highly compressible soil below the foundation level is removed within the stressed zone – or in part of it.
Soil replacement: out with the bad soil – in with the good

We modify the foundation itself: a larger footing area reduces the contact pressure, the foundation level is taken deeper, or the poor soil below the foundation level is replaced with better soil.

If the calculated settlements are not acceptable, the original design has to be changed. The methods can be combined – the choice depends on the subsoil, the depth of the intervention and the cost. The page follows this order: within the four groups the subsections (1/A, 1/B …) follow one another.
